did_you_know.text: Did you know? After the plague, the Lord commanded Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron to conduct a new census of the Israelites.
Did you know? The census included men twenty years old and upward who were eligible for military service, and it was organized by ancestral households and families.
Did you know? Although Korah’s sons are mentioned alongside Dathan and Abiram and Korah’s rebellion, the Torah explicitly states: “The sons of Korah did not die.”
Did you know? Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
Did you know? The total number of Israelites counted in this census was 601,730.
Did you know? The division of the land was based on the size of the families: a larger family received a larger inheritance, and a smaller family received a smaller inheritance.
Did you know? Although the size of each inheritance was determined by the number of people counted, the location of each tribe’s inheritance was determined by lot.

Did you know? The Levites were counted separately from the Israelites, and all the males among them aged one month and older numbered 23,000; they were not included in the census of those eligible for military service and received no inheritance within Israel.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, it is stated that none of the generation counted in the wilderness of Sinai remained, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
